0.name: Bypass-capacitor
0.guide: Can be recycled at e-waste centers. May contain harmful dielectric materials—do not dispose in regular trash.

1.name: Electrolytic-capacitor
1.guide: Contains liquid/gel electrolytes—handle carefully and recycle at specialized e-waste facilities.

2.name: Integrated-micro-circuit
2.guide: Should be removed from circuit boards and sent to certified electronic refining plants.

3.name: LED
3.guide: Do not throw in trash. Recycle at e-waste facility. May contain trace amounts of gallium, arsenic, or lead.

4.name: PNP-transistor
4.guide: Contains semiconductors. Recycle with other discrete electronics or at e-waste drop-offs.

5.name: armature
5.guide: High scrap metal content (copper windings, steel shaft). Recycle at metal recovery or e-waste yards.

6.name: attenuator
6.guide: May contain resistive carbon or ceramic materials—send to e-waste recycling.

7.name: cartridge-fuse
7.guide: Contains metal alloy filaments and glass/ceramic cartridges. Recycle through specialized facilities.

8.name: clip-lead
8.guide: Metal and PVC/rubber components—sanitize and reuse if intact, otherwise route to cable recycling.

9.name: electric-relay
9.guide: Contains copper coils, silver contact points, and plastics. Recycle responsibly for precious metals.

10.name: filament
10.guide: Typically found in specialized vacuum or incandescent equipment—recycle through lighting programs.

11.name: heat-sink
11.guide: Made of extruded aluminum or copper—valuable scrap metal. Highly recyclable at metal scrap facilities.

12.name: induction-coil
12.guide: Contains high-purity enameled copper wire. Extract and recycle for copper reclamation.

13.name: jumper-cable
13.guide: Reusable wire harnesses. If damaged, strip for insulated copper wire recycling.

14.name: junction-transistor
14.guide: Semiconductor device. Group with silicon-based components for e-waste processing.

15.name: light-circuit
15.guide: Printed circuit sub-assembly—the entire sub-board should be sent to PCB refining.

16.name: limiter-clipper
16.guide: Circuit wave-shaping network—recycle alongside PCB waste streams.

17.name: local-oscillator
17.guide: RF oscillator module—handle with PCB waste or salvage quartz crystal resonators.

18.name: memory-chip
18.guide: Contains precious metals (gold wire bonding, copper). Certified e-waste refiners can reclaim metals.

19.name: microchip
19.guide: Silicon IC with packaging—do not throw in municipal trash. Recycle with e-waste.

20.name: microprocessor
20.guide: High value CPU—refine for gold, silver, and copper recovery with professional electronic recyclers.

21.name: multiplexer
21.guide: Logic/analog IC switch—route to electronic scrap sorting.

22.name: omni-directional-antenna
22.guide: Inspect for physical reuse. Broken antennas should be recycled for brass/copper/aluminum.

24.name: potentiometer
24.guide: Variable resistor. Test for reuse or recycle for copper wipers and resistive tracks.

25.name: pulse-generator
25.guide: Timing/pulse module—recycle with small electronic assemblies.

26.name: relay
26.guide: Electromechanical switch containing copper coil and contacts—disassemble or recycle at e-waste facility.

27.name: rheostat
27.guide: Heavy-duty variable wirewound resistor—salvage ceramic core and nickel-chromium or copper resistance wire.

28.name: semi-conductor
28.guide: General semiconductor package—recycle at specialized e-waste electronic plants.

29.name: semiconductor-diode
29.guide: Small two-terminal semiconductor—recycle as part of board-level e-waste.

30.name: shunt
30.guide: Precision low-resistance current sensor (often manganin or brass)—valuable alloy recycling.

31.name: solenoid
31.guide: Contains heavy copper wire electromagnetic coil—recycle for copper and ferrous core recovery.

32.name: stabilizer
32.guide: Power regulation unit with transformers and control boards—drop off at bulk e-waste collection points.

33.name: step-down-transformer
33.guide: Heavy transformer—recycle for iron laminations and primary/secondary copper windings.

34.name: step-up-transformer
34.guide: High-voltage transformer—do not scrap in general trash. Recycle for copper and silicon steel.

35.name: transistor
35.guide: General transistor package—recycle with electronic components.
